findings.title: Stream-end before the dispatch's own result still returns partial text as success
findings.description: `_read_turn()` maps `StopAsyncIteration` to `None` at `src/squadron/pipeline/sdk_session.py:302-303`, but `_collect_turns()` only raises when `turns.ledger.active` is true (`src/squadron/pipeline/sdk_session.py:234-239`). If the SDK stream ends before any `ResultMessage` — or after only an injected result — and no background task is active, line `src/squadron/pipeline/sdk_session.py:240` returns `turns.text()` as a successful dispatch even though `turns.own_result_seen` is still false. That produces a silent partial/empty success with no WARNING/ERROR log or `ProviderError`, contradicting the dispatch contract at `src/squadron/pipeline/sdk_session.py:184-187` and the required observable signal for a new stream failure mode.

findings.title: Discarded leftover turns leak background ledger state into the next dispatch
findings.description: When an injected result arrives before the current dispatch's own result, `src/squadron/pipeline/sdk_session.py:243-251` calls `turns.discard()` and continues. `DispatchTurns.discard()` only clears `parts` (`src/squadron/pipeline/sdk_turns.py:130-134`); it leaves `BackgroundLedger._active` and `_seen` populated from `observe()` (`src/squadron/pipeline/sdk_turns.py:55-65`, `src/squadron/pipeline/sdk_turns.py:71-83`). A leftover follow-up turn carrying `TaskStartedMessage`/`TaskUpdatedMessage` therefore leaks active tasks and `seen_count` into the current dispatch, which can inflate `background_tasks_waited` at `src/squadron/pipeline/sdk_session.py:212-213`, trigger waiting/idle-timeout logic at `src/squadron/pipeline/sdk_session.py:219-229`, or stop the wrong tasks. The added leftover-turn test only uses text and a result message, so it does not cover this lifecycle-message leak.

findings.title: Config file boundary accepts wrong types and bools as ints
findings.description: `load_config()` merges raw TOML values directly into the config dictionary without per-key schema validation (`src/squadron/config/manager.py:82-102`). The new typed accessor fixes `bool` reads with `isinstance(value, bool)` (`src/squadron/config/manager.py:130-133`), but the `int` branch still uses `if not isinstance(value, int)` (`src/squadron/config/manager.py:134-137`), so Python's `bool`-is-an-`int` subclassing lets `True` pass as an integer; the float branch at `src/squadron/config/manager.py:138-140` has the same problem. A hand-edited `"pipeline.background_idle_timeout_s" = true` therefore reaches `asyncio.timeout()` through `src/squadron/pipeline/sdk_session.py:323-327` and `src/squadron/pipeline/sdk_session.py:300-301` as a one-second timeout, and negative/zero values are not rejected at the boundary. The Python rules require Pydantic validation for file-parsing boundaries and fail-fast validation, not runtime trust in untyped TOML values.

findings.title: Async session paths perform blocking config I/O on the event loop
findings.description: `_collect_turns()` is an `async def` and calls `_background_idle_timeout_s()` at `src/squadron/pipeline/sdk_session.py:224`. That helper calls `get_typed_config()`, which reads both user and project TOML files through `open()`/`tomllib.load()` (`src/squadron/config/manager.py:47-52`, `src/squadron/config/manager.py:82-102`) and can trigger legacy config migration via `shutil.copytree()` (`src/squadron/config/manager.py:19-34`). `open_pipeline_session()` also calls `get_typed_config()` twice, each call reloading the config files. This is synchronous disk I/O inside await-able code and can exceed the required <1ms worst case, blocking all loop I/O while a dispatch is waiting on background agents. Resolve these settings once at session construction or move the file read off the event loop with an explicit async boundary.

findings.title: New background-task timeout path has no load-tier test
findings.description: `SDKExecutionSession.dispatch` now adds persistent-client stream waiting, repeated `receive_response()` passes, `asyncio.timeout()`, `stop_task()`, and background-task accounting. The added tests are scripted unit tests; `TestBackgroundIdleTimeout` uses a fake `ScriptedClient` with short `0.15`/`0.05` sleeps and asserts functional logs/counts. `tests/load` still contains only unrelated cases such as `tests/load/test_worktree_concurrency.py:1-50` and `tests/load/test_grep_timeout.py`, with no realistic-configuration test asserting latency, throughput, or resource bounds for SDK dispatch waiting. `.github/workflows/ci.yml:38` runs `uv run pytest`, so a `tests/load/` case would be gated; the Python rules require at least one load test for this concurrency/network/environment-layer path.

findings.title: Blanket exception suppression bypasses the project's exception-handling rule
findings.description: `_stop_background()` uses `except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001`, logs with `_logger.exception()`, and then continues without re-raising (`src/squadron/pipeline/sdk_session.py:333-341`). This is not a specific exception type, not a re-raise after logging, and not a documented top-level process-boundary handler, while the `noqa` disables the mechanical BLE enforcement. The handler is observable at ERROR level, but it can also swallow programming errors from `stop_task()` (e.g. `TypeError`/`AttributeError`) as if they were cleanup failures. If the SDK truly exposes no narrower type, wrap `stop_task()` in a small adapter that raises a typed domain error and catch only that, or re-raise after logging.
